content_units: Double-Feature Game Plan
I built three mood-based pairings from your 10-film list, each kept under   240 minutes total   and chosen to feel distinct rather than interchangeable.
Mood-Matched Pairings
Mood   Pair   Total Runtime   Why it works
Uplifting     Paddington 2   +   Hunt for the Wilderpeople       204 min     Warm, funny, emotionally generous films with adventurous momentum and a big-hearted payoff.
Brainy     Arrival   +   Ex Machina       224 min     A clean sci-fi double bill focused on language, consciousness, identity, and the human cost of intelligence.
Tense-but-not-disturbing     Knives Out   +   The Nice Guys       246 min     Great tonal fit, but this pairing runs over your limit, so I replaced it below.
Best Final Set Under Your Time Limit
1) Uplifting:  Paddington 2  +  Hunt for the Wilderpeople
-   Runtime:   103 + 101 =   204 minutes
-   Why this pairing works:   Both movies are funny, humane, and deeply charming without feeling lightweight.
-   Energy arc:    Paddington 2  starts with pure sweetness and clever comedy;  Wilderpeople  keeps the warmth but adds more wild adventure and emotional growth.
-   Shared appeal:   lovable outsiders, found-family themes, and a lot of heart.
-   Best for:   when you want to end the night in a great mood.
2) Brainy:  Arrival  +  Ex Machina
-   Runtime:   116 + 108 =   224 minutes
-   Why this pairing works:   This is your strongest “ideas first” double feature.

-   Pairing logic:    Arrival  is expansive, emotional, and philosophical;  Ex Machina  is tighter, colder, and more probing. Together they explore communication, intelligence, and what makes someone truly human.
-   Energy arc:   begin with awe and reflection, then narrow into psychological tension and ethical ambiguity.
-   Best for:   a conversation-heavy night where you’ll want to talk afterward.
3) Tense-but-not-disturbing:  Knives Out  +  Palm Springs
-   Runtime:   130 + 90 =   220 minutes

-   Why this pairing works:    Knives Out  gives you suspense, momentum, and puzzle-solving fun without getting grim.  Palm Springs  keeps the cleverness and tension around repetition/time-loop stakes, but stays breezy and entertaining.
-   Pairing logic:   both are structurally playful, fast-moving, and smart, with tension softened by humor.
-   Energy arc:   start with a satisfying whodunit, then shift into a lighter but still clever late-night reset.
-   Best for:   wanting suspense and mental engagement without ending on something heavy or upsetting.
Pairing Logic at a Glance
Why these three stand out
-   Uplifting   works best when both films are emotionally generous, not just funny.
-   Brainy   works best when both films are idea-driven and complementary rather than repetitive.
-   Tense-but-not-disturbing   needs suspense with wit, style, or lightness so it never becomes oppressive.
Good films that almost made it
-   Spirited Away   is a great uplifting option, but pairing it under 240 minutes while keeping the same mood purity is trickier.
-   Spotlight   is brainy, but its subject matter makes the overall evening heavier.
-   Zodiac   is excellent, but it pushes “tense” into a much darker, more unsettling zone.
-   The Nice Guys   fits the lighter-suspense mood well, but runtime constraints make it harder to pair cleanly.
